parityFailure.testName: S1 live migration parity > verifies every checkpoint read-only, or explicitly generates only after semantic proofs pass
parityFailure.assertion: expect(columns.find(column => column.table_name === table.name && column.name === nullablePrimary[0])).toMatchObject({ type: 'text', notnull: false })
parityFailure.rootCauseFact: migrations/postgres/0027_privacy_purge_events.sql line 4 declares event_id text NOT NULL CONSTRAINT privacy_purge_events_nullable_pk UNIQUE, and line 23 comments that constraint as ccc:sqlite-primary-key. The harness requires a column carrying that marker to be nullable, because the SQLite counterpart migrations/sqlite/0071_privacy_purge_events.sql line 3 declares event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, and a SQLite TEXT PRIMARY KEY accepts NULL. The NOT NULL on the PostgreSQL side makes the two dialects disagree on that single column.
parityFailure.precedent: every earlier table using this marker omits NOT NULL on the marked column, for example migrations/postgres/0008_audio_objects.sql lines 16, 45, 63 and 69 declare id text CONSTRAINT <name>_nullable_pk UNIQUE with no NOT NULL. The same marker also appears in 0001_baseline.sql, 0004_agent_jobs.sql and 0007_consent_six_domains.sql.
parityFailure.diagnosticRerun: one extra read-only run was made because the assertion carries no label, then the table and column were identified from the migration files themselves. Same failure both times.
